title: Breeding-tier colored text on 8–15% tier tints fails in both themes (1.97–4.12:1)
description: Active breeding pills set color: var(--sr-tier-N) over rgba(var(--sr-tier-N-rgb), 0.08–0.15) composited on the card surface. Computed over --sr-surface: LIGHT — tier-1 text on tier-1@0.15 = 2.32:1 (any active tier-1 code pill, and the 'Possible' filter pill in BirdingStats); DARK — tier-4 text 1.97:1 (the active 'Confirmed' category pill), tier-3 text 2.94:1, tier-2 text 4.12:1, tier-2-on-tier-1-tint 3.53:1. Same defect at BreedingCodeList.tsx:58-60 (category pills), SpeciesDetail.tsx:786-788 (breeding category pill), BirdingStats.tsx:1637-1638 (Confirmed/Probable/Possible filter pills). Related same-root-cause case: the white badge count on the tier-2 circle (BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219) is 3.96:1 in dark (tier-2 lightened to #A855F7) while passing in light (5.38:1).
fix: Introduce --sr-tier-N-fg tokens per theme for text-on-tint (dark theme needs the text far lighter than the fill tokens; light theme tier-1 needs the existing --sr-tier-1-text dark purple), and extend the tier-1-text pattern to the dark-mode tier-2 badge circle (dark text on #A855F7 would pass).

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran all contrast math independently (alpha-compositing tints over --sr-surface with globals.css token values): every claimed ratio reproduces exactly (light tier-1 2.32:1; dark tier-4 1.97, tier-3 2.94, tier-2 4.12, tier-2-on-tier-1 3.53; badge 3.96 dark / 5.38 light), and pill text is 12px/500 so the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies. The pairs genuinely co-occur in codePillStyle (line 45) and categoryPillStyle (lines 58-60) active states, plus the cited BirdingStats:1626/1637-1638, SpeciesDetail:786-788, and BreedingCodeTable:219 locations, all verified in current code. ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this — it affirmatively claims filter pills meet 4.5:1 in both themes, so 'serious' is the right severity; the suggested --sr-tier-N-fg fix matches the existing --sr-tier-1-text both-themes token precedent and I verified dark #1A0030 on dark tier-2 #A855F7 = 4.88:1 passes.

title: Help overlay: fixed 200px TOC sidebar never collapses — content column collapses to ~30px at 320px width
description: The HelpDocs body lays the TOC and content side by side with inline styles only — no media query and no wrap. The TOC is `width: 200, flexShrink: 0`, the row adds `padding: '0 24px'` and `gap: 40`, so at a 320 CSS px viewport (e.g. 1280px window at 400% zoom, or a phone) the help content column gets roughly 320 − 48 − 200 − 40 ≈ 32px. Markdown text wraps at one or two characters per line (long words overflow), making the in-app documentation effectively unreadable exactly for the low-vision users most likely to need it. Every other layout in the app handles this (globals.css has a 640px media query; TabNav measures and collapses), so this is the one true reflow failure found. It also contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 ("The layout reflows for narrow windows and at large sizes … without clipping content").
fix: Below a narrow-width breakpoint (~700px), stack the TOC above the content (flexDirection column) or move it behind a disclosure button. A `.sr-help-body` class plus a rule in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css is the smallest change; alternatively reuse the TabNav measurement pattern.

verdict.reasoning: HelpDocs.tsx lines 341-351 lay out the TOC (inline width:200, flexShrink:0) and content (flex:1, minWidth:0) with gap 40 and 0 24px padding, all inline styles with no className, and globals.css's only width media block (640px) has no help-overlay rules — so at 320 CSS px the content column is ~32px as claimed. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 affirmatively claims reflow works (exempting only tables/maps), so this is contradicted rather than disclosed. Severity serious is fair: the in-app documentation becomes unreadable at 400% zoom for exactly the low-vision users it serves.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested .sr-help-body class + rule in the existing @media (max-width: 640px) block is right, but because the layout is inline styles the override needs !important (the existing block already does this pattern for .sr-header's inline padding) — e.g. add classes to the row and nav and rule `.sr-help-row { flex-direction: column !important; gap: 0 !important; } .sr-help-toc { width: 100% !important; position: static !important; max-height: none !important; }`. The existing 640px breakpoint is sufficient for SC 1.4.10 (failure threshold is 320 CSS px); no new ~700px breakpoint needed.

title: --sr-text-disabled used for real content text (2.29–2.56:1)
description: The disabled-text token (#A1A1AA light = 2.56:1 on surface, 2.45:1 on bg; #52525B dark = 2.29:1 on surface, 1.93:1 on surface-subtle) is widely used for meaningful, non-disabled content: Settings file sublabels (Settings.tsx:240) and full explanatory paragraphs (Settings.tsx:1143, 1174), file dates (:235), tab-layout 'HIDDEN' labels (:739), Species Detail counters and zero values (SpeciesDetail.tsx:461, 584, 690, 830, 926), comparer '—' and italic placeholders that convey 'no value' (ChecklistComparer.tsx:100, 534), the List Comparer section label (ListComparer.tsx:203), and the LifeList 'no filter' chip (LifeList.tsx:606). The WCAG inactive-control exemption does not apply to any of these — they are informative text.
fix: Replace --sr-text-disabled with --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark on surface) everywhere the text is content rather than a label inside a genuinely disabled control; reserve the disabled token for disabled buttons/inputs only.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the WCAG math independently: every reported ratio is exact (light #A1A1AA on #FFFFFF = 2.56:1, on #F9FAFB = 2.45:1; dark #52525B on #18181B = 2.29:1, on #27272A = 1.93:1; muted = 4.83/6.91 on surface). The cited Settings.tsx sites (235, 240, 250, 388, 739, 1143, 1174) are informative content — file dates, sublabels, status chips, explanatory paragraphs — none inside a disabled control, so the 1.4.3 inactive-control exemption does not apply. ACCESSIBILITY.md's contrast section claims AA for body text and discloses only chart-bar labels, not this; serious is the right severity for sub-2.6:1 body-size content text.
verdict.fixNote: Swapping to --sr-text-muted is right for most sites, but light-theme muted (#71717A) on --sr-surface-subtle (#F4F4F5) is only 4.40:1 — just under AA. The 'No file saved' / 'No key saved' chips (Settings.tsx:250, 388) sit on surface-subtle, so for those either use --sr-text (or a new AA-checked token added to BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css) or lighten the chip background; all other cited Settings sites are on --sr-surface or --sr-bg where muted passes (4.83:1 / 4.62:1 light, 6.91:1+ dark).

title: axe color-contrast: 139 runtime instances in light theme, traceable to ~4 token-level causes
description: axe-core rule `color-contrast` (impact: serious), 139 violating nodes across all 10 tabs at default (light) theme, deduped by failing color pair: (a) --sr-accent #2D8653 (globals.css:29) used as small text fails by a hair on every light surface — 4.32:1 on #f9fafb (active tab label in TabNav, all 10 tabs), 4.03:1 on #e8f5ee accent-bg (selected segmented/sort buttons, 24x), 4.11–4.33:1 on #f4f4f5/#fafafa (links, 9x); (b) --sr-text-muted #71717A (globals.css:18) on --sr-surface-subtle #f4f4f5 = 4.39:1 — the 66 "Jump to section" nav pills (BirdingStats.tsx:450) and similar chips; (c) --sr-text-disabled #A1A1AA (globals.css:19) used for INFORMATIVE text at 2.33–2.56:1 — result-count announcements ("87 comments" aria-live spans in Checklists/LifeList), empty date-input text (color: var(--sr-text-disabled) at SpeciesDetail.tsx:638 etc.), "267 species" counts — worst offenders; (d) chart/inline labels: hardcoded white 10px % labels on --sr-graph-photo #3B82F6 bars = 3.67:1 (BirdingStats.tsx:1153, 5x) and on --sr-graph-video #8B5CF6 = 4.23:1; --sr-tier-1 #C084FC 1.5rem-bold breeding "Possible" count on white = 2.64:1, below even the 3:1 large-text threshold (BirdingStats.tsx:1613); --sr-accent-border-strong text "Loaded from Settings" on accent-bg = 2.52:1 (ListComparer); Settings date-format sublabels 3.16–3.33:1.
fix: Token-level fixes in globals.css :root — darken --sr-accent to ~#277448 (≥4.5 on #f4f4f5) and --sr-text-muted to ~#65656e; stop using --sr-text-disabled for informative text (counts, date values) — switch those to --sr-text-muted; for chart labels either darken the bar fills the white text sits on or move labels outside the bars; use --sr-tier-1 only for swatches, not text, or pair the tier-1 stat with a darker text token.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed every claimed pair and all match within 0.03 (accent 4.32/4.03/4.11/4.33 as small text incl. the 0.875rem/500 TabNav active label; muted 4.40 on the verified jump pills; disabled 2.33-2.56 confirmed on informative text at Checklists.tsx:177/668 aria-live counts, SpeciesDetail.tsx:638, Settings sublabels; white-on-#3B82F6 3.68 at BirdingStats.tsx:1153; tier-1 2.64 at :1613; accent-border-strong 2.53 at ListComparer.tsx:258). ACCESSIBILITY.md discloses only the chart-bar percentage-label subpart and otherwise claims AA for text/buttons/links in both themes, which the accent/muted/disabled items contradict, so not treated as disclosed. Proposed fixes verified: #277448 yields 5.09-5.46 and #65656e yields 5.25 on the cited surfaces; token-level :root changes fit conventions (dark theme has its own values).

title: Dark theme: white chip/badge text on lightened recency-tier fills fails badly (1.52–1.92:1)
description: tierColors() hardcodes text:'white' for the fresh and mid recency tiers, but the dark-theme tokens lighten those fills (--sr-map-target-fresh #34D399, --sr-map-target-mid #6EE7B7). Computed: white on #34D399 = 1.92:1, white on #6EE7B7 = 1.52:1 (dark); even light-theme mid (#5EA07C) is only 3.09:1. These colors carry the species-name label on every Media Targets map chip (TargetMarkers.tsx:72, 11px/600) and the '≤7 days' tier badge in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:100, 10px/600) — the primary content of the Map Explorer's Media Targets mode is near-unreadable in dark mode. The 'old' tier already does this right (--sr-map-target-old-text adapts per theme, 4.86:1 light / 10.83:1 dark).
fix: Add per-tier text tokens like the existing --sr-map-target-old-text (e.g. --sr-map-target-fresh-text / -mid-text: white in light where the fill is dark enough, dark green like #052E16 in dark where the fills are pastel) and return them from tierColors() instead of the literal 'white'.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran WCAG math: white on dark-theme #34D399 = 1.92:1 and #6EE7B7 = 1.52:1 (light-theme mid #5EA07C = 3.09:1), all failing 4.5:1 for the 11px/600 chip text (TargetMarkers.tsx:72) and 10px/600 tier badge (line 100) that carry the Media Targets mode's primary content. tierColors() at mapExplorerFormat.ts:61-62 hardcodes 'white' while the old tier already uses a per-theme --sr-map-target-old-text token, confirming the asymmetry. ACCESSIBILITY.md's only disclosed contrast exception is chart-bar labels and it claims map popups meet AA, so this is undisclosed; serious is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested per-tier text tokens are correct and convention-conforming (define in both :root and [data-theme="dark"]); make explicit that --sr-map-target-mid-text must be dark in the LIGHT theme too (white on light-mid #5EA07C is only 3.09:1, failing 4.5:1 at 11px), while --sr-map-target-fresh-text can stay white in light (#2D8653 = 4.52:1) and go dark (e.g. #052E16) in dark.

title: ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim is broader than the computed reality
description: The published statement says text, buttons, links, map popups and form controls 'meet the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standard (4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes', with chart-bar labels as the only known exception. Computed counterexamples outside that exception: light-theme active pills/links on tinted backgrounds 4.03–4.41:1 (accent-on-accent-bg, error-on-error-bg, active tab on page bg), --sr-text-disabled used on content at 2.29–2.56:1, dark-theme target chips at 1.52–1.92:1, dark-theme breeding pills at 1.97–2.94:1, and form-control borders at 1.19–1.27:1 (non-text). The repo treats this file as a published statement whose claims must be true; today it overstates. (Verified-true parts: the tier-1 badge example, the recency-dot hidden labels, the text-footer/sci-name token fixes, focus-ring contrast, and the dark-mode popup theming.)
fix: Either fix the token-level failures in this report (most are 1-line token edits) and keep the claim, or temporarily widen the known-exceptions paragraph to honestly cover active-state tints in light theme and chip/pill labels in dark theme.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited ratios independently and each one holds with co-occurring real UI: light accent-on-accent-bg 4.03 / error-on-error-bg 4.41 (LifeList.tsx:107-108 active pills) / active tab on bg 4.32 (TabNav.tsx:94); --sr-text-disabled 2.29-2.57 on non-disabled content (Settings.tsx:240/376 sublabels); dark target chips 1.52/1.92 (white text hardcoded in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:61-62); dark breeding pills 1.97-2.94 after alpha-blending the 0.08 tints (BreedingCodeList.tsx:43-60); borders 1.19-1.27. ACCESSIBILITY.md:31 claims AA in both themes with only the chart-bar-label exception, so the published statement is overstated — and CLAUDE.md explicitly requires this file's claims to stay true. The only stated exception does not cover any of these, so alreadyDisclosed is false.
verdict.fixNote: The two-option fix is sound, with one correction: the dark-theme target-chip failure is not a token edit — lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts hardcodes text: 'white' (itself against the no-hardcoded-colors convention). Fix it like the existing old-tier pattern: add --sr-map-target-fresh-text / --sr-map-target-mid-text tokens to BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css and reference them, mirroring --sr-map-target-old-text. The breeding-pill fix likewise needs the dark-theme tier text colors lightened (or pill text switched to --sr-text) rather than tint-alpha tweaks, since the 0.08 tint barely moves the blended background. Any token change must land in both theme blocks per convention; ACCESSIBILITY.md edits alone need no version bump.

title: Map chrome text inherits MapLibre's fixed `font: 12px/20px Helvetica` — does not scale with the in-app Text Size control
description:
maplibre-gl.css (imported at SnowMap.tsx:7) sets `.maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,…}`. The app's `.maplibregl-popup-content` override in globals.css:568 themes colors but sets no font-size or family, so any map-rendered text without an explicit rem size stays at a hard 12px Helvetica regardless of the Text Size setting. Affected: (1) the AtlasLayer block popup title — `
{sel.name}
` at AtlasLayer.tsx:213 and the linked variant at :208-211 have no fontSize; (2) the attribution credits on every map (SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}` — provider links render at fixed 12px when expanded); (3) the AtlasLayer popup's default close button (it is the only popup that doesn't pass `closeButton={false}`, so users get maplibre's small fixed-size '×' — also a WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size concern). This matters more here than in a typical web app: ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 states the Text Size control is "especially useful in the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own", so on desktop this text is genuinely un-resizable. All other popups (SightingMarkers, HotspotMarkers, TargetMarkers, SightingsMap, the BirdingStats geo popup) set explicit rem sizes and are fine.
fix: In globals.css extend the existing popup override: `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`; give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize; pass `closeButton={false}` on the AtlasLayer popup for consistency with the other four popups (its onClose path already exists).

verdict.reasoning: Every claim checks out: maplibre-gl.css sets .maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,...}, the globals.css:568 popup override adds no font-size/family, the AtlasLayer block name (:208-213) has no fontSize, .maplibregl-ctrl-attrib inherits the fixed 12px, and the Text Size control scales only rem text via html{font-size:calc(100% * var(--sr-text-scale))} (globals.css:378). On desktop — which ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 itself says has no browser zoom — this text is un-resizable, a genuine 1.4.4 failure there (web is saved by browser zoom); at 200% the popup title would render smaller than its own muted secondary text. AtlasLayer is indeed the only popup of six without closeButton={false}, but that part of the fix is wrong (see fixNote).
verdict.fixNote: The CSS parts are right: extend the existing globals.css override with `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`, and give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize (e.g. 0.8125rem). But do NOT pass closeButton={false} on the AtlasLayer popup: it also sets closeOnClick={false}, so the default close button is its only dismiss affordance and its only keyboard-operable control — removing it would strand the popup open and worsen 2.1.1. Instead keep the button and size it via the existing .maplibregl-popup-close-button override (e.g. add `font-size: 1rem; padding: 2px 8px;`), which also addresses the 2.5.8 target-size concern.

title: Hardcoded milestone-chip and rank-icon colors below AA (2.76–4.16:1), bypassing the token system
description: The Firsts & Milestones chips hardcode hex colors (also violating the project's tokens-only rule): the tier-1 date link #5EA07C on #E8F5EE = 2.76:1 (10px text), tier-1 number #2D8653 on #E8F5EE = 4.03:1, tier-2 date #3E7A56 on #D8EDE4 = 4.16:1 (tier-3/4 pass: 4.92–6.37:1). These values are identical in both themes since the chips don't adapt. Separately, RankIcon (statsPrimitives.tsx:97-98) prints white 10px-bold rank numbers on hardcoded #3B82F6 = 3.68:1 (the #2D8653 circle squeaks by at 4.52:1).
fix: Move the milestone palette into --sr-* tokens and darken the failing fg values (date ≥ #43755C on #E8F5EE; num → --sr-accent-strong); for RankIcon use --sr-chart-blue-dark (#1D4ED8, 6.70:1 under white) as the square fill.

verdict.reasoning: Hardcoded hexes verified at BirdingStats.tsx:671-677 and statsPrimitives.tsx:95-98 (violating the CLAUDE.md tokens-only rule), and my recomputation matches: tier-1 date 2.76:1 and tier-2 date 4.16:1 at 10px (need 4.5), RankIcon white-on-#3B82F6 3.68:1 at 10px bold (need 4.5). One overstatement: the tier-1 threshold number is 1.25rem/700 = 20px bold = WCAG large text, so its 4.03:1 PASSES at the 3:1 large-text threshold — the real failures are the two date links and the RankIcon square. Still a fair moderate: real sub-AA text plus a standing-convention violation.
verdict.fixNote: Tokenize the milestone palette into --sr-milestone-* tokens defined in BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] (globals.css), darkening only the failing date colors (tier-1 date >= #43755C on #E8F5EE = 4.76:1, tier-2 date similarly); the tier-1 number (20px bold = large text) already passes at 4.03:1 >= 3:1 and needs no change. Do NOT use var(--sr-chart-blue-dark) for the RankIcon square as suggested — it resolves to #3B82F6 in the dark theme, which is 3.68:1 under the white 10px-bold rank text and still fails; instead add a dedicated token (e.g. --sr-rank-square: #1D4ED8 in both themes, 6.70:1 under white) and use var(--sr-accent... ) tokens for the circle.

title: Disclosed chart-bar-label exception verified — but it understates the dark-theme failures (down to 1.29:1) and a working fix already exists in-code
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md's known exception ('a few dense data-visualization labels (percentage figures printed inside saturated chart bars) do not yet meet AA in every case') is accurate in direction but materially understates scope. Computed: LIGHT — white on --sr-graph-audio 2.15:1 (protocol bar), white on --sr-chart-slate 2.56:1, white on --sr-graph-photo 3.68:1, white on --sr-graph-video 4.23:1. DARK — --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light 1.29:1 (comment/species-notes bars, BirdingStats.tsx:1384/1405), white on graph-audio 1.44:1, white on --sr-accent 1.92:1 (hardcoded '#fff' at protocol bar :1181), white on graph-photo 2.54:1, white on chart-slate 2.56:1, --sr-text on chart-slate 2.33:1 (:1361), white on chart-blue-dark 3.68:1 (:1125). In dark mode it is most in-bar labels, not 'a few'. Notably, line 1358 already uses var(--sr-on-accent) which passes in BOTH themes (4.52/7.75) — the failures are the literal '#fff' and var(--sr-text) usages that don't adapt.
fix: Replace literal '#fff' bar-label colors with per-fill adaptive tokens (the existing --sr-on-accent pattern), or render the percentage outside/beside the segment when the segment color can't carry AA text; then tighten the ACCESSIBILITY.md wording to match whatever remains.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed every cited pair with my own WCAG relative-luminance implementation; all match (dark --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light = 1.29:1 at lines 1384/1405, white on dark graph-audio 1.44, white on dark accent 1.92 via the hardcoded '#fff' at 1181, dark text-on-slate 2.33 at 1361, white on dark chart-blue-dark 3.68 at 1125), and line 1358's --sr-on-accent does pass both themes (4.52/7.75) proving the fix pattern exists in-code. Labels are 11-12px weight-600, so the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies — in dark mode most in-bar labels fail, some catastrophically, which materially exceeds the 'a few cases' wording in ACCESSIBILITY.md line 31. Confirmed at moderate: the percentages are supplemental (raw counts appear in the adjacent header text), but 1.29:1 is effectively invisible text.

title: DropZone error state's border and icon are nearly invisible (1.74–1.90:1)
description: In the error state the drop zone's border and upload icon switch to --sr-error-muted (#FCA5A5 light): 1.74:1 against the --sr-error-bg fill and 1.90:1 against the surrounding surface, so the state-change boundary/icon fails non-text contrast (dark: icon vs surface 2.74:1; vs error-bg 3.02:1 passes). The role=alert error text is present, but it itself is the marginal 4.41:1 light error-on-error-bg pair reported separately.
fix: Use --sr-error (#DC2626) for the error-state border and icon — 4.41:1 vs error-bg and 4.83:1 vs surface, comfortably over the 3:1 non-text bar.

verdict.reasoning: DropZone.tsx lines 39-43 and 108 set the error-state border and icon to --sr-error-muted on --sr-error-bg; my own WCAG luminance math reproduces every reported ratio (light 1.74:1 vs error-bg, 1.90:1 vs white surface; dark 2.74:1 vs surface, 3.02:1 vs error-bg), confirming a 1.4.11 failure in light theme and a marginal dark theme. The role=alert text partially conveys the state, so moderate is the right severity. The suggested var(--sr-error) fix is verified in both themes (4.41/4.83:1 light, 7.07/6.40:1 dark) and follows the --sr-* token convention; note it must be applied at both line 40 (border) and line 108 (icon).

title: DropZone inline `outline: 'none'` defeats the global keyboard focus ring
description: The DropZone (role="button", tabIndex=0 — keyboard activation itself works) sets outline: 'none' in its inline style. Inline styles override the stylesheet's [role="button"]:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sr-accent) } rule (globals.css:546-551, no !important), leaving only the rule's faint 12%-alpha box-shadow glow as the focus indicator; the border/background highlight is driven by mouse-only isHovered state. Keyboard users on the List Comparer get an almost invisible cue on the primary upload control. (Reported here because it directly degrades keyboard operation of an otherwise-correct widget; full focus-visible sweep belongs to that dimension.)
fix: Delete the inline outline: 'none' (the global :focus-visible ring only shows for keyboard focus, so the mouse aesthetics are unaffected), or mirror the isDragging accent border on :focus-visible.

verdict.reasoning: Line 69's inline outline:'none' overrides globals.css:542-551's [role="button"]:focus-visible / [tabindex]:focus-visible ring (no !important), leaving only the rule's rgba(45,134,83,0.12) box-shadow (~1.05:1 over the light surface, effectively invisible), and the component has no focus-driven styling of its own — isHovered is mouse-only. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md's claim that every focused control shows a clear green outline, so it is not a disclosed exception. An effectively absent focus indicator on the List Comparer's two upload controls is a real 2.4.7 AA failure, understated at minor; the suggested fix (delete the inline outline:'none') is correct and safe since :focus-visible does not fire on mouse interaction.

title: 'Personal Location' popup badge fails in light theme (2.90:1)
description: The hotspot popup's 'Personal Location' badge sets --sr-map-personal (#C9842A) text on --sr-is-target-bg (#FFF7ED): 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 (dark passes, 8.38:1). The pin color token was designed as a map fill, not a text color.
fix: Use --sr-is-target-text (#C2410C, 4.88:1 on that bg) or --sr-warning for the badge text in light theme.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed: #C9842A (--sr-map-personal) on #FFF7ED (--sr-is-target-bg) = 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 — small text, fails the 4.5:1 AA minimum exactly as reported; dark theme (#E0A060 on #1C0F00) = 8.38:1, passes. HotspotMarkers.tsx:156 matches the finding, and the badge is the popup's only textual indicator that the pin is a personal location, so it is meaningful text — moderate stands. Not disclosed: ACCESSIBILITY.md affirmatively claims map popups meet AA and lists only chart-bar percentage labels as the known exception.
verdict.fixNote: Swap color: 'var(--sr-map-personal)' for 'var(--sr-is-target-text)' unconditionally — no light-theme branch needed, since the token is theme-scoped (4.88:1 light, 8.30:1 dark, both pass) and --sr-is-target-bg + --sr-is-target-text is already the codebase's badge pairing (LifeList.tsx:529).

title: Light theme: muted text on tinted surfaces falls just under AA (4.27–4.40:1)
description: --sr-text-muted #71717A passes on white (4.83:1) but not on the tinted surfaces it is commonly paired with in light theme: on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.40:1 (inactive segmented-control labels in MapSidebarUI SegControl, the basemap switcher buttons in globals.css:246, the missing-media badges in the target popup TargetMarkers.tsx:92, numerous chips); on --sr-quote-bg = 4.27:1 (Named Birds comment block); on --sr-accent-bg = 4.31:1 (secondary text inside selected rows, e.g. the location line of a selected Nearest Targets row, MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317). Dark theme passes all three (5.27–5.82:1).
fix: Darken light --sr-text-muted to ~#6B6B74 (≈4.6:1 on #F4F4F5) — a single token change; verify it still reads as 'muted' next to --sr-text.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG math confirms the ratios: #71717A is 4.397:1 on #F4F4F5, 4.268:1 on #EFF1F3, and 4.310:1 on #E8F5EE (dark theme passes 5.27-5.82), and the surface-subtle and accent-bg pairings genuinely co-occur at small text sizes (SegControl inactive labels MapSidebarUI.tsx:13+24, basemap switcher globals.css:234/246, TargetMarkers.tsx:92 badges, selected-row secondary text MapSidebarUI.tsx:96+109 and MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317); these are enabled controls, so the inactive-component exemption does not apply. One cited pairing is wrong: the quote-bg comment blocks (NamedBirdRow.tsx:110, Checklists.tsx:350-351) use full-contrast --sr-text, not muted, so that instance never occurs — but the finding stands on the other two surfaces. The proposed #6B6B74 verifies as passing everywhere (4.66-4.80 on the tinted surfaces, 5.28 on white), and changing only the :root value is convention-clean since the token already exists in both themes; not covered by ACCESSIBILITY.md's chart-bar-label exception.

title: List Comparer summary bars and result panels don't reflow at 320px — labels truncate to identical text
description: Both comparer results screens use rigid column counts with no narrow-width collapse. The five-cell summary (`gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 1fr)'` — ResultsView.tsx:111 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:281) gives each cell ~58px at 320px; the 0.625rem uppercase labels are `whiteSpace: nowrap; overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis` (ResultsView.tsx:165-173, ChecklistComparer.tsx:478), so "Checklist A" and "Checklist B" (and "<name> total" pairs) ellipsize to identical strings — the numbers become indistinguishable at that width. Below them, ResultsView.tsx:129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` species panels and ChecklistComparer.tsx:310 `1fr 1fr` A-only/B-only panels never stack, leaving ~90-140px columns where species names wrap to 4+ lines. Nothing scrolls two-dimensionally and the panel headers repeat the counts, so it is degraded rather than lost — but the summary labels' ambiguity is a concrete information loss at 320px.
fix: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` for the stat bars (cells wrap to two rows on narrow screens), and collapse the panel grids to one column under 640px (reuse the `.sr-two-col` media-query pattern from globals.css:601).

verdict.reasoning: Verified all cited lines: ResultsView.tsx:111 `repeat(5, 1fr)` with nowrap/ellipsis 0.625rem labels (165-176), :129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` panels, and the ChecklistComparer twins (281, 310, ~479) — all inline styles with zero responsive handling (no matchMedia, no media-query class) anywhere in ResultsView/ListComparer/ChecklistComparer. At 320px each stat cell is ~55-64px with 40px horizontal padding, leaving ~15-24px for the label (1-3 chars + ellipsis): 'Checklist A'/'Checklist B' and filename-derived labels (eBird exports share the 'MyEBirdData' prefix) truncate to identical strings — concrete information loss under SC 1.4.10, though the both/A-only/B-only counts are duplicated in the panel headers so only the two totals become truly ambiguous. Moderate is the right severity: real AA failure at 320px/400% zoom, but degraded rather than blocking.
verdict.fixNote: The stats-bar half of the fix is sound (rem-based `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` inline also scales with the in-app Text Size control). The panel half won't work as written: the grids' `gridTemplateColumns` are inline styles, and a media-query class rule cannot override an inline declaration — move the grid definition into a class (as SpeciesDetail.tsx:802 uses `className="sr-two-col"` with no inline grid). ResultsView's panel grid is 3 columns, so `.sr-two-col` isn't directly reusable: either add an `.sr-compare-panels { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) }` base rule with a `1fr` override in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css (the ChecklistComparer's 1fr-1fr grid CAN reuse `.sr-two-col` directly), or skip media queries entirely with inline `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr))`. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 currently claims narrow-window reflow 'without clipping content' — it should be corrected or the fix shipped to keep that published statement true.

title: Light theme: accent-colored text marginally fails on tinted/page backgrounds (4.03–4.32:1)
description: Light --sr-accent #2D8653 passes on white surfaces (4.52:1) but fails where it is used on anything tinted: on --sr-accent-bg = 4.03:1 — the app-wide active-state pattern (ghost buttons, active filter pills, the tab dropdown's selected option TabNav.tsx:309-314, SpeciesPanel count badge :44-45; background:'var(--sr-accent-bg)' + accent text appears in 14 files); on --sr-bg = 4.32:1 — the active tab label (tab bar sits directly on the page background, App.tsx:583) and the footer 'Up to date' status (App.tsx:1154); on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.11:1. Dark theme passes everywhere (7.75–10.35:1).
fix: In light theme use --sr-accent-strong (#1A5C38; 7.12:1 on accent-bg, ~6.7:1 on bg) for accent-as-TEXT on tinted/page backgrounds, keeping --sr-accent for fills, borders and focus rings; or darken light --sr-accent to ~#27764A so it clears 4.5:1 on --sr-accent-bg.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG relative-luminance math reproduces every reported ratio exactly: light #2D8653 is 4.03:1 on --sr-accent-bg #E8F5EE, 4.32:1 on --sr-bg #F9FAFB, 4.11:1 on --sr-surface-subtle #F4F4F5 (4.52:1 on white passes; dark theme passes at 7.75-10.35). The pairs genuinely co-occur — dropdown selected option (TabNav 309-314), SpeciesPanel count badge (11px accent text on accent-bg), active tab label over the body's --sr-bg background, footer 'Up to date' span — all normal-size text requiring 4.5:1, and 24 files reference --sr-accent-bg. ACCESSIBILITY.md claims AA for primary interface colors with only chart-bar labels excepted, so this is a real undisclosed AA failure; the suggested --sr-accent-strong fix is convention-compliant (token defined in both themes; verified 7.12:1 on accent-bg, 7.64:1 on bg) and the alternative #27764A verifies at 4.96/5.32/5.56.

title: ToggleSwitch off-state track is nearly invisible in light theme (1.48:1)
description: The off-state track uses --sr-gray-400 (#D4D4D8): 1.48:1 against the white button surface AND 1.48:1 against the white knob, so the knob position — the visual state indicator of every 'merge subspecies' / 'show spuh' / 'hide weather' switch — is barely discernible in light theme (the on state passes: accent track 4.52:1 vs surface). Dark theme: track vs surface 2.29:1 (also <3:1) though knob-vs-track passes (7.73:1). aria-checked is correct for AT, but the sighted off/on distinction fails non-text contrast.
fix: Darken the light off-track (e.g. #8E8E96 ≈ 3.1:1 on white and vs the white knob) and lighten the dark off-track (e.g. #6E6E78), or add a 1px --sr-border-medium-darkened outline to the track and knob.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed all ratios from globals.css tokens and they match exactly: light off-track #D4D4D8 is 1.48:1 vs both the white surface and the white knob (knob position imperceptible), on-track 4.52:1, dark track 2.29:1 vs surface with knob-vs-track 7.73:1. ACCESSIBILITY.md claims form controls meet AA contrast and discloses only chart-bar labels, so this is not a known exception. Moderate is right: a genuine 1.4.11 failure on a widely-used control, but state remains inferable from green-present/absent (state-vs-state 3.06:1) and aria-checked is correct for AT.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested hexes verify (#8E8E96 = 3.25:1 on white; #6E6E78 = 3.51:1 vs dark surface, 5.04:1 vs white knob), but '--sr-border-medium-darkened' does not exist and hardcoded hexes in the component would violate the --sr-* token rule. Since --sr-gray-400 has no other consumers, either retune --sr-gray-400 to #8E8E96 (:root) / #6E6E78 ([data-theme="dark"]) in frontend/src/globals.css, or — cleaner, since #8E8E96 would be oddly dark for a 'gray-400' slot — add a dedicated --sr-toggle-off-track token in BOTH themes and reference it at ToggleSwitch.tsx:27. Also update the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim if the fix doesn't ship immediately.

title: Dark theme: map pin tokens are lightened 'for dark backgrounds' but draw on the always-light Positron basemap (1.69–2.25:1)
description: There is no dark basemap variant (lib/mapStyle.ts tunes Positron only; no theme branch), yet the dark-theme --sr-map-* tokens lighten the pin colors: visited/heat pins #34D399 vs Positron land (~#F2F0EB) = 1.69:1, personal #E0A060 = 1.97:1, unvisited #7BA7C9 = 2.25:1 (light theme passes: 3.66–3.97:1). The GL circle/teardrop sprites read these tokens at runtime (map/SightingMarkers.tsx:80, lib/mapPins.ts, HotspotMarkers sprites), so switching the app to dark mode makes the primary map markers fainter against the unchanged light tiles. White glyphs inside the dark-theme teardrops also drop below 3:1 (star on #E0A060 = 2.24:1, dots on #7BA7C9 = 2.56:1). Mitigation: the sidebar in-view lists duplicate marker info, which keeps this from serious.
fix: Anchor the on-map pin tokens to the basemap, not the app theme (keep the light-theme values in dark mode, or add a dark halo/outline to the GL sprites); keep the lightened values only for sidebar legend dots that actually sit on dark surfaces.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the mechanism end-to-end: lib/mapStyle.ts has no dark basemap variant (Positron only), SightingMarkers.tsx reads --sr-map-visited via useCssToken at runtime (theme-reactive per the data-theme MutationObserver contract), and my recomputation matches exactly — dark tokens #34D399/#E0A060/#7BA7C9 hit 1.69/1.97/2.25:1 on ~#F2F0EB land, with white teardrop glyphs at 2.24/2.56; the pin strokes are hardcoded white (SightingMarkers.tsx:160, mapPins.ts:133) so they add no edge contrast on light tiles. One inaccuracy: light theme does NOT fully pass — --sr-map-personal #C9842A is only 2.70:1 on the land tint, so the personal pin fails 1.4.11 in both themes. ACCESSIBILITY.md documents the sidebar keyboard path to markers but not marker contrast, so not disclosed; the sidebar mitigation keeps moderate the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: Add dedicated basemap-anchored pin tokens (e.g. --sr-map-pin-*) defined with the SAME values in both :root and [data-theme="dark"] for the GL circle layer and sprite bakes, keeping the existing --sr-map-* for sidebar legend/list dots on app surfaces. Note 'keep the light-theme values' alone is insufficient: light --sr-map-personal #C9842A is itself 2.70:1 on the land tint, so pair the shared pin tokens with a dark stroke ring — replace the hardcoded #ffffff circle-stroke-color (SightingMarkers.tsx:160) and sprite strokeStyle '#fff' (mapPins.ts:133) with a dark outline to supply the 3:1 boundary against light tiles.

title: No skip link to bypass the header/tab bar before main content
description: There is no skip-to-main-content link anywhere in the app (grep for skip-link patterns across src/, index.css, App.css, globals.css, and main.tsx returns nothing). The branding header (App.tsx:570) and TabNav (App.tsx:583) render before <main> (App.tsx:586). Impact is low — strictly, 2.4.1 is satisfiable via the existing <main> landmark (technique ARIA11), the header contains no focusable elements, and both TabNav variants are a single tab stop (desktop roving tabindex at TabNav.tsx:132; collapsed dropdown is one trigger button) — so a sighted keyboard user pays only one extra Tab per page load. Reported as a best-practice gap rather than a conformance failure.
evidence: App.tsx:570 header div and :583 <TabNav> precede <main> at :586; no element or CSS class implementing a skip link exists in the codebase.
suggestedFix:
Add a visually-hidden-until-focused anchor as the first child of the root div: Skip to main content, give
id="sr-main" and tabIndex={-1}, and style .sr-skip-link to appear on :focus (positioned fixed, z-index above 1200 since overlays use 1200).

verdict.reasoning: Verified: no skip link exists anywhere in src/ or index.html; header (App.tsx:570) has no focusable elements, both TabNav modes are one tab stop, and <main> (App.tsx:586) provides a landmark, so 2.4.1 is technically satisfied (ARIA11) and the cost is one extra Tab. The auditor honestly framed it as a best-practice gap and rated it minor, which is correct — landmarks help AT users but not sighted keyboard users, so a skip link is the standard remaining piece. Fairly-flagged polish item, not pedantry.
verdict.fixNote: Suggested fix is sound; style .sr-skip-link with var(--sr-*) tokens added to both :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css (per the theming convention), and z-index above 1200 as noted since the map fullscreen overlay and dropdown both sit at 1200.

title: Multi-series line charts differentiated by hue alone
description: The media-over-time chart draws four lines (photo/audio/video/total) distinguished only by stroke color, with a color-keyed legend — for color-blind users the photo (blue) vs video (purple) pair in particular is hard to separate. Tooltips name each series on hover and the role="img" summary covers AT users, so the information is reachable, but not glanceable. Same pattern wherever SightingsGraph's media chart overlays multiple series.
fix: Add per-series strokeDasharray patterns and/or distinct dot marker shapes to the recharts <Line> elements so series differ by more than hue.

verdict.reasoning: Lines 1775-1778 of BirdingStats.tsx render four <Line> series with dot={false}, no strokeDasharray, and only stroke color differentiating them; Vienot protan/deutan simulation collapses the photo #3B82F6 / video #8B5CF6 pair from RGB distance 88.6 to ~1-2 (same in dark theme #60A5FA/#A78BFA), confirming the confusion claim. SightingsGraph.tsx's media overlay (lines ~157-172) is likewise hue-only (its dots are same-shape circles in the series color). Hover tooltips and the role=img label keep the info reachable, so minor severity is correctly stated.
verdict.fixNote: Add per-series strokeDasharray to the four <Line>s in BirdingStats.tsx (e.g. photo solid, audio '6 3', video '2 3', total '8 3 2 3'); since dot={false} there, dashes are the practical cue. Apply the same patterns to the photo/audio/video overlay in speciesDetail/SightingsGraph.tsx (~lines 157-172). Note recharts' default Legend line icon does not render the dash pattern, so either pass a custom legend `content` or distinct `legendType` icons so the legend also differs by more than hue. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md currently claims 'Color is never the only way information is conveyed' — update it (or fix the charts in the same change) per the CLAUDE.md rule that it must stay true.

title: Chart non-text elements below 3:1: amber line in light theme, faint bar segments, stacked-segment boundaries
description: Computed non-text chart parts under 3:1 — light theme: the Audio series line --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs the white card = 2.15:1 (media-over-time chart; SightingsGraph media line too), --sr-chart-blue-light bar segment vs surface = 1.80:1, tier-1 fill vs surface = 2.64:1; the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments: tier-2 vs tier-1 = 2.04:1 light / 1.50:1 dark, tier-4 vs tier-2 = 2.79:1 light / 2.20:1 dark (BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679). Mitigations keeping this minor: every chart has a data-bearing role="img" label, tooltips, and most values are duplicated as text (legend counts, BarRow numerals).
fix: Darken light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1 — already proven in --sr-age-immature), add 1px separators between stacked-bar segments, and bump light --sr-chart-blue-light/tier-1 fills toward their 3:1 neighbors.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited non-text ratios and they match: light --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs white 2.15:1 (media LineChart at :1776), --sr-chart-blue-light vs white 1.80:1, tier-1 vs white 2.64:1, and the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments at :1677-1679 (tier-2/tier-1 2.04 light / 1.50 dark; tier-4/tier-2 2.79 / 2.20). The stated mitigations are real (role="img" summaries at :557/:1266/:1755, legends, BarRow prints value+pct as text), which correctly keeps this at minor under 1.4.11's redundant-presentation allowance — the amber series line is the strongest genuine instance since the lines themselves carry the trend.
verdict.fixNote: Darkening light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1, matches light --sr-age-immature) is verified and safe. But do NOT shift the shared --sr-tier-* palette to fix the stacked-bar boundaries — those tokens drive the map atlas overlay, hatch sprites (--sr-tier-N-rgb), legend parity, and the breeding-badge dark-text-on-light-tier pairing called out in ACCESSIBILITY.md; instead add 1px var(--sr-surface) gaps between the three stacked segments at BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679, which fixes segment distinguishability with zero blast radius.

title: Light theme: error text on error background is just below AA (4.41:1)
description: --sr-error #DC2626 on --sr-error-bg #FEF2F2 computes to 4.41:1 — marginally under 4.5:1 — and this pair styles every error banner and the 'negative' filter pill state: Checklists.tsx:236/488, LifeList.tsx:108/384, BreedingCodeList.tsx:196, Settings.tsx:304/480, ChecklistComparer.tsx:374, NamedBirds.tsx:108, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:186, SpeciesDetail.tsx:430, DropZone.tsx error text. Dark theme passes (7.07:1). Error on plain surface also passes (4.83:1), so only the tinted-banner pair needs a nudge.
fix: Darken light --sr-error slightly (e.g. #D31F1F ≈ 4.8:1 on #FEF2F2) or introduce an --sr-error-text token used on --sr-error-bg; one token edit in globals.css fixes all listed locations.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the pair co-occurs (Checklists.tsx:236 TriPill 'no' state and :488 error banner, plus the other listed files) and re-computed the ratio: #DC2626 on #FEF2F2 = 4.415:1, a genuine but marginal AA miss at 13px text; dark theme (7.07:1) and plain-surface (4.83:1) pass as the finding states. The 0.085 shortfall is perceptually negligible and light-theme-only, so 'moderate' overstates user impact — this is a compliance nudge, not a barrier; downgrading to minor. The fix is validated (#D31F1F = 4.82:1 on #FEF2F2, 5.27:1 on white) and convention-compliant as a single light-theme token edit in globals.css.

title: 'No media' minus icon nearly invisible (1.47:1 light / 1.70:1 dark)
description: Life List media columns render a Minus icon in --sr-gray-300 (#D1D5DB) on the white row surface = 1.47:1 (dark: #3F3F46 on #18181B = 1.70:1) to mean 'no media of this type' (repeated at lines 288, 302, 316, 331). The meaning ('zero') is inferable from the absence of a count link, which is why this is minor rather than moderate, but the chosen glyph as drawn fails non-text contrast in both themes.
fix: Use --sr-text-disabled or --sr-border-medium darkened to ≥3:1, or render a plain '—' in --sr-text-muted (which also gives AT users something to announce).

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed independently: --sr-gray-300 on --sr-surface is #D1D5DB/#FFFFFF = 1.47:1 light and #3F3F46/#18181B = 1.70:1 dark — exactly as reported, at lines 288/302/316/331, well under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11. Minor is the right severity since the absent count link redundantly conveys 'zero'. Not covered by ACCESSIBILITY.md's lone known exception (chart-bar percentage labels).
verdict.fixNote: Two of the finding's three suggested tokens fail its own 3:1 target: --sr-text-disabled computes to 2.56:1 light / 2.29:1 dark, and --sr-border-medium to 1.73:1 / 1.70:1 (its dark value IS #3F3F46, the currently-failing color). Use the third option only: color the glyph var(--sr-text-muted) (#71717A light = 4.83:1, #A1A1AA dark = 6.91:1; token already defined in both themes), either keeping the <Minus> icon or rendering a text em dash — the text variant additionally gives screen readers something to announce.

title: Four inline `animation: 'spin …'` styles in MapExplorer bypass the .spin class convention
wcag: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (policy per ACCESSIBILITY.md) — regression-risk only, no current failure
description: MapExplorer.tsx applies the spinner keyframes via inline style objects instead of the shared `.spin` class at four sites: line 657 (map loading chip, 'spin 1s linear infinite'), line 682 ('Locating…' spinner, 'spin 0.7s linear infinite'), line 1003 and line 1224 (hotspots / media-targets 'Finding…' spinners, 'spin 1s linear infinite'). There is NO current user impact: the reduced-motion kill in globals.css:588-594 uses a universal `*` selector with `!important` longhands, and author !important declarations override inline styles, so these spinners are correctly frozen for reduced-motion users today. The risk is silent regression: these are the only animations in the codebase that escape the `.spin` class, so any future refactor that scopes the RM block to classes (e.g. `.spin { animation: none }`) instead of `*` would leave these four spinning for reduced-motion users with nothing failing visibly. Reported once; all four locations listed here.
fix: Replace the inline `animation:` declarations with `className="spin"` at MapExplorer.tsx lines 657, 682, 1003, and 1224 (matching every other spinner in the app), so all spinner motion flows through the one class the reduced-motion CSS is built around.

verdict.reasoning: All four inline animation:'spin' sites exist as cited and a repo-wide grep confirms they are the only spinners bypassing the .spin class (line 1438 of the same file uses it). The reduced-motion block (globals.css:588-594) is `*` + !important longhands, which does override inline styles, so the finding's no-current-failure, regression-risk-only framing is accurate and fairly flagged against the published reduced-motion commitment in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: Suggested fix is correct and convention-aligned. One caveat: .spin runs at 0.7s while lines 657/1003/1224 use 1s, so adopting the class slightly speeds those three spinners — cosmetic and consistent with the rest of the app; line 682 already matches 0.7s.

title: Recency tier is color-alone at a glance (sighted users); the faint 'old' dot compounds it in light theme (1.64:1)
description: The fresh/mid/old recency tiers on the Nearest Targets sidebar dots and the on-map chip backgrounds are differentiated only by color for sighted users; the sr-only labels (MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313) cover screen readers — so ACCESSIBILITY.md's specific claim about hidden labels on recency dots is TRUE — and the popup shows the tier as text ('≤7 days') plus the date, so the information is reachable by interaction. But a color-blind user scanning the list/map cannot rank targets without clicking each one, and the light-theme 'old' dot (#A8D4BB) is also only 1.64:1 against the sidebar surface (its compensating border is --sr-border at 1.27:1).
fix: Show the visible date (already computed) or a tier letter/shape next to each sidebar dot, and give the 'old' dot a ≥3:1 border (e.g. --sr-accent-strong).

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the WCAG math: light-theme --sr-map-target-old #A8D4BB vs the sidebar's var(--sr-surface) #FFFFFF is 1.64:1 and the dot's --sr-border #E4E4E7 border is 1.27:1 — the reported ratios are exact (the 'old' tier takes the var(--sr-border) border branch at :1310 since its text token isn't 'white'). The sidebar row (:1310-1319) shows name/location/distance but no date or tier text, and the on-map chips (TargetMarkers.tsx) are colored by tier only, so the tier IS color-alone at a glance for sighted users; the sr-only labels (:1311-1313) and the popup's '≤7 days' text + date exist as the finding accurately concedes. Minor is fair given the interaction path, and the fix is valid: --sr-accent-strong exists in both themes (globals.css:30/:131) and is 7.98:1 against the light surface.

title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: sub-24px targets (species favicon links, combobox chevron)
description: The eBird and Birds of the World favicon links rendered next to every bird name are 14×14 px targets with a 5 px gap — under the 24×24 minimum, packed in dense table rows where the spacing exception doesn't obviously hold, and they appear hundreds of times (Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Stats). The SpeciesDetail chevron (~16 px, SpeciesDetail.tsx:521) is similar. Not a WCAG 2.1 AA failure; flagged as a 2.2 delta.
fix: Grow the anchor hit area to ≥24×24 via padding on .sr-favicon-slot (visual size can stay 14px), and give the chevron button a 24px hit box.

verdict.reasoning: Same favicon facts verified independently (largely a duplicate of finding 67's part (a)): 14x14 anchor hit areas with a 5px gap (centers 19px apart < 24px, so the spacing exception fails), rendered via BirdName across Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, and Stats. Correctly framed as a 2.2 delta, not a 2.1 AA failure; minor stands and ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose it. The chevron half is weaker: the full-width 40px combobox input opens the dropdown on focus/click (SpeciesDetail.tsx onFocus handler), so the ~16px chevron plausibly meets 2.5.8's Equivalent exception.
verdict.fixNote: Padding on .sr-favicon-slot works (the anchor wraps the slot, so the anchor's hit area grows); pair it with a matching negative margin so dense table rows don't widen, and keep the img at 14px (the slot's fixed-size layout-shift guard comment in globals.css still holds if width/height become the padded total). The chevron 24px hit box is optional — it is arguably exempt under the 2.5.8 Equivalent exception since the 40px-tall input toggles the same dropdown.

title: Bird-name links replace the standard focus ring with only a color change + underline
wcag: 2.4.7 Focus Visible AA (weak indicator; 2.4.13 Focus Appearance fail forward-looking)
description: `.sr-birdname-link:hover, .sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; outline: none; }` — the class rule out-specifies the global `button:focus-visible` outline, so the most common interactive element in the app (every species name in Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Map Explorer, Statistics, comparer rows) shows only a green tint + underline on keyboard focus, identical to the mouse hover style. In a dense table of hundreds of rows this is materially harder to track than the 3px ring used everywhere else, and it weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim of a 'clear green outline' wherever focus lands. The global rule's faint 12% box-shadow still applies but contributes almost nothing.
fix: Split the selector: keep `outline: none` for :hover only, and let :focus-visible keep (or restore) the global outline alongside the color/underline — e.g. `.sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; }` with no outline override.

verdict.reasoning: Rule verified verbatim at globals.css:306; BirdName renders a <button class="sr-birdname-link"> with no other focus styling, and the (0,2,0) class selector beats the (0,1,1) global button:focus-visible ring, leaving only color+underline plus the near-invisible 12%-alpha box-shadow. However keyboard focus still produces a clearly visible change (4.18:1 color shift plus an underline appearing), so WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 technically passes and 2.4.13 Focus Appearance is AAA in WCAG 2.2 — this is a real consistency issue that also contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'clear green outline' claim, but not an AA failure, so moderate overstates it.
verdict.fixNote: No selector split needed: just delete `outline: none` from the combined rule — `.sr-birdname-link:hover, .sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; }`. Hover never paints an outline on a non-focused element, and the suggested split's `:hover { outline: none }` would suppress the ring whenever a focused name is also hovered; with the override gone, the global `button:focus-visible` 3px ring applies on keyboard focus only.

title: Form-control borders are far below non-text contrast (1.19–1.34:1)
description: --sr-border (#E4E4E7 light / #27272A dark) is the only boundary cue on text inputs, selects, date inputs and unselected pills throughout the app (SELECT_STYLE here; the same '1px/1.5px solid var(--sr-border)' pattern on inputs in MapExplorer, Checklists, LifeList, Settings, SpeciesDetail). Computed: 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark vs surface, 1.21:1 / 1.34:1 vs page bg; even --sr-border-medium is 1.73:1 light / 1.70:1 dark. Inputs whose extent is identified only by this border fail 1.4.11; the focus ring fixes it only once focused.
fix: Introduce an --sr-border-input token at ≥3:1 vs surface (≈#949499 light, ≈#5F5F66 dark) for form-control boundaries, or give inputs a contrasting filled background (--sr-surface-subtle is itself only 1.07:1 vs surface, so the border route is simpler).

verdict.reasoning: Re-computed all ratios and they match: --sr-border vs surface is 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark (1.21/1.34 vs page bg), --sr-border-medium 1.73/1.70 — the borders are near-invisible. But the W3C Understanding of 1.4.11 does not require a visible boundary when the control is otherwise identifiable, and every cited control carries a placeholder ('Search by place name', 'Paste your API key', 'e.g. 37.8275') and/or a visible label, and SELECT_STYLE selects show a ~4.7:1 chevron glyph — so this is a genuine low-vision usability weakness, not a clear normative AA failure. Confirmed as a worthwhile polish fix at minor severity rather than moderate.
verdict.fixNote: The --sr-border-input token approach is right (define in both :root and [data-theme="dark"]), but the suggested dark value #5F5F66 is only 2.80:1 vs --sr-surface #18181B — below the fix's own 3:1 target. Use ~#6B6B73 (3.35:1) or #707078 (3.61:1) for dark; light #949499 passes at 3.02:1 but only barely, so a slightly darker value gives margin.

title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all claims: 26 inline outline:'none' occurrences match the listed locations, inline style beats the non-!important outline in globals.css:556-563, and only the !important border-color plus the stylesheet box-shadow survive — the designed 2px ring never renders on these controls. However the surviving indicator (1.5px border flipping gray→accent at 4.52:1 light / 9.22:1 dark vs surface, plus a 4px glow, with explicit onFocus borderColor handlers in Settings) is a perceivable, conventional focus treatment, so 2.4.7 AA is not actually failed — the finding itself concedes this. Real as an app-wide design-consistency issue that also makes ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs' claim inaccurate, but a non-failing degradation grades as minor, not moderate.
